editor.noTargets: You have no targets yet. Add one under the Targets tab first.

kindBlurb.detection: A person, vehicle or animal the camera saw. Narrow it by class, zone, face or plate; everything else is optional.
kindBlurb.sensor: A doorbell press or a linked sensor changing state. The picture comes from the camera the sensor is attributed to.
kindBlurb.sound: Fires on a confirmed window of audio, never on a picture. Name the sounds and/or keep a level threshold — with neither it can never match.
kindBlurb.occupancy: Fires when the count in a camera frame or a zone crosses your threshold and holds. Pick the camera first — the zone list is that camera's.
kindBlurb.device-events: A device or its stream going away or coming back, switched off or on, a battery or consumable running low, a camera with motion but nothing detected, motion without a subject. There is no frame to attach.
kindBlurb.system: The installation itself: a node leaving, an addon crash-looping, an update available or installed, a backup or an export finishing.
kindBlurb.alarm: The alarm panel: refused, arming, armed, entry delay, triggered, re-armed, sensor bypass, disarmed.
kindBlurb.mixed: This rule mixes events from more than one family (device events, system, alarm). It keeps firing as it is, but it can no longer be edited: create one rule per family, then delete this one.

editor.dropTitle: These will be removed when you save
editor.dropHint: This kind of rule can't use them, so keeping them would leave the rule silent.
editor.notForTriggerHint: Not evaluated for the selected trigger — switch the trigger to use it.
editor.gifHint: A short animation cut from the live buffer around the moment — the camera does not have to be recording.
editor.clipHint: An MP4 of the same cut. Destinations that take no video still get the picture.
editor.templateHint: Leave both blank for the hub's own wording.
editor.noCameras: No cameras available — the rule applies to all devices.
editor.devicesUnavailable: The hub did not return its cameras — selected ones are listed by id so they can still be removed.
editor.devicesEmptyWidens: No camera selected: the rule will apply to ALL cameras.

plates.offHint: The rule does not care about the plate — a vehicle whose plate could not be read matches too.
plates.anyKnownHint: Only vehicles whose plate was actually read, whatever it said.
plates.specificHint: Only these plates, matched tolerantly — plate reading is never perfect.

systemFilters.summaryClassHint: At the scheduled time you get the list of what is in the bad state, not each change.
systemFilters.instantClassHint: A paired event tells you both when it goes wrong and when it comes back.
systemFilters.cameras: Only when triggered by these cameras (optional)
systemFilters.excludeHint: Applied after the list above: a device here is never reported, whatever else matches.
systemFilters.batteryTypesWarning: Battery and consumable alerts are narrowed by device type here. Batteries and consumables belong to sensors, containers, vacuums and mowers — rarely to a camera — so a type filter meant for liveness silences them. Leave the types empty, or put these kinds in a device rule of their own.
systemFilters.thresholdsHint: The battery threshold and reminders are cluster settings (admin UI → post-analysis settings). A consumable’s threshold is this rule’s own.
systemFilters.consumableThresholdHint: This rule is told when a consumable’s remaining life reaches this percentage (empty = {{defaultPercent}}%). Another rule may use its own number — each is told at its own threshold. A device that reports “replace” is announced whatever this says.
systemFilters.consumableThresholdInvalid: A whole number from {{min}} to {{max}} — this value is not saved.
systemFilters.alarmTriggeredMedia: When a rule sets the alarm off, this notification carries that rule's pictures.

crossing.enterHint: Entries and ordinary movement; never an exit.
crossing.exitHint: Only an exit from a zone.

editor.deviceStateNone: Not set — this rule is never gated on another device.
editor.deviceStateSet: Only while device {{deviceId}} is: {{states}}. Change it from the admin UI — this app cannot list every device.

occupancy.zonesNeedCamera: Pick the cameras above to choose one of their zones.
occupancy.zonesNone: These cameras have no zones — the count covers the whole frame.
occupancy.zoneMissing: Zone "{{id}}" no longer exists on these cameras. The rule still stores it and will never fire until you pick another scope.
occupancy.classesNone: The hub sent no class vocabulary — the count covers every class.
occupancy.classMissing: "{{name}}" is not a class these cameras report. The rule still stores it and will never fire until you pick another one.
occupancy.sustainInstantHint: A 0-second hold fires on the very first frame that crosses — expect repeat notifications from a subject that walks the edge of the zone. 15 seconds is the usual choice.
occupancy.hint: Counts confirmed tracked objects from zone analytics. The change must hold for the whole window before it fires; with no snapshot for the camera or zone the rule never fires.
occupancy.classesDropped: The class filter ({{classes}}) is dropped on save: an occupancy edge carries one class, so it would only stop this rule from ever firing. Scope the class above instead.

audio.modeLabelHint: Fires when enough labelled frames land inside a short window (default 2 in 5 seconds). A single-frame false positive never reaches 2; a real episode usually labels two or three frames. The rule's cooldown is the other throttle.
audio.modeLevelHint: Fires when the sound stays loud enough for long enough: the window below is the whole condition.
audio.labelsHint: Pick at least one. The classifier labels only a frame or two per episode, so a percentage of a window could never confirm them — this mode counts those frames instead.
audio.confirmHitsHint: How many labelled frames must land inside the window before a notification is sent. Default 2 — a single-frame false positive never reaches it.
audio.confirmWindowHint: The window those frames must share. Default 5 s. Two frames six seconds apart do not confirm.
audio.labelsUnknown: This rule stores {{labels}}, which this hub does not classify. It is kept as-is; tap it to drop it.
audio.dbHint: dBFS is negative-going: 0 is full scale, −96 is silence — so a HIGHER number is a NARROWER filter. Measured on this hub, a baby crying reads −55 to −26 dBFS, so a floor above −55 excludes most of it.
audio.hitPercentHint: How much of the window must match before it fires. Default 60%.
audio.samplingHint: The window must be FULL before it can match — a half-open window never fires. Default 10s.
audio.failClosedHint: Pick at least one sound or set a level floor. With neither, every sample is a hit and the hub refuses the rule rather than notifying on silence.
audio.hint: Fires on sustained SOUND, not on a picture: a rule with this condition is evaluated only on a confirmed audio window, never on a detection or a track. The cameras it covers need audio analysis enabled.

zonePicker.needCamera: Select a camera first — zones belong to a camera.
zonePicker.none: The selected cameras have no zones.
zonePicker.missing: Zone {{id}} no longer exists on the selected cameras

occupancy.sensorKinds: An occupancy edge is not a sensor event: it carries no sensor kind, so this condition can never match one.
occupancy.eventTypeTokens: An occupancy edge carries no device event-type token — that comes from an event emitter, which a count crossing has none of.
occupancy.source: An occupancy edge is always produced by the pipeline, so any other source can never match and “pipeline” narrows nothing.
occupancy.sensorTransition: An occupancy edge is a count crossing, not a sensor reading: it has no raise or clear, so this choice could never narrow it.

sound.classes: A sound rule fires on what the camera HEARD. Its subject carries no detection, so this condition can never match one — name the sounds in the Sound condition instead.
sound.classesExclude: A sound rule fires on what the camera HEARD. Its subject carries no detection, so there is nothing here to exclude — name the sounds in the Sound condition instead.
sound.minConfidence: A sound window’s evidence is a percentage of samples, not a detector score, so a confidence threshold can never be satisfied.
sound.zones: A sound has no position in the frame, so a zone can never match it.
sound.zonesExclude: A sound has no position in the frame, so a zone can never exclude it.
sound.customZones: A sound has no position in the frame, so a drawn area can never match it.
sound.crossing: A sound has no position in the frame, so it can never cross a zone boundary.
sound.labelEquals: A sound rule fires on what the camera HEARD. Its subject carries no detection and therefore no label — name the sounds in the Sound condition instead.
sound.identities: A sound rule fires on what the camera HEARD. Its subject carries no detection, so there is no face to recognise.
sound.identitiesExclude: A sound rule fires on what the camera HEARD. Its subject carries no detection, so there is no face to exclude.
sound.plates: A sound rule fires on what the camera HEARD. Its subject carries no detection, so there is no plate to read.
sound.source: A confirmed sound window is always stamped as an audio subject, so any other source can never match.

sensor.sensorTransition: Only a sensor that raises and clears (water, smoke, gas, CO, vibration, tamper, motion, contact) can fire on one edge. Pick only such sensor kinds, or the rule fires on every change.

detection.audio: A detection rule fires on what the camera saw. Sounds are a Sound rule of their own.

ai.enabledHint: Adds one sentence written by a vision model to this notification. It never withholds the notification — if the model is cold or unreachable, the alert is delivered without the sentence.

blurb.occupancy: The model is shown the still and told the count this rule claims, and answers whether that count holds. Your question guides what it looks at; the verdict sentence is written by the hub, so a disagreement always says so.
blurb.detection-immediate: The model is shown the still taken at the moment this rule fired and answers your question about it.
blurb.detection-track: The model is shown the beginning, the best moment and the end of the passage, and answers your question about what happened across them.

ai.noProfiles: No vision-capable model is configured on this hub. Add one from the admin Settings before switching this on.
ai.profilesUnavailable: This hub cannot list its vision models. The section still saves; the hub picks its own default model.
ai.maxWordsHint: About how many words to ask for. It is an instruction to the model, not a cut — expect roughly this length, occasionally a word or two over. Unset, this rule's targets give {{words}}.
ai.maxWordsVaries: About how many words to ask for. It is an instruction to the model, not a cut. Your targets do not agree on a default; the strictest of them gives {{words}}, and unset each target gets its own.
ai.occupancyContract: The answer stays a verdict: the hub asks for the count, compares it with this rule's, and writes the confirmation or the refutation itself. Your question guides the model — it cannot change the answer's format.

unsaved.body: This rule has changes that are not saved.

editor.missing: This rule no longer exists. It may have been deleted.
editor.fixedTrigger: Trigger: {{trigger}} — a sensor rule fires on the device event itself.

actions.securityNote: These actions run on your devices when the rule is switched on or off, when it fires, or when someone taps one of its buttons. Check every one before saving.
actions.deviceSearchPlaceholder: Search by name, room or id
actions.deviceUnavailable: The hub did not return its devices — the list cannot be shown right now.
actions.capUnavailable: The device's capabilities could not be read. Type the capability name.
actions.methodHint: The capability method to call, e.g. setState or trigger.
actions.argsHint: Each argument is checked when you save. JSON takes objects and lists.
actions.buttonsHint: A button on the notification that runs one shared sequence.
actions.destructiveHint: Draws the button in red. It changes how it looks, not who may press it.
actions.sequencesHint: Sequences are created in the admin console, under Notifications → Sequences. Here a rule only runs them.
actions.sequencesNone: The hub has no sequence yet. Create one in the admin console (Notifications → Sequences) to run it here or from a button.
actions.sequencesUnavailable: The hub's sequences could not be read — they are shown by id.
actions.unknownSequences: Sequences this rule runs that no longer exist on the hub: {{count}}. They will not run.

onActivation.title: On activation
onActivation.hint: Runs when the rule is turned on.

onDeactivation.title: On deactivation
onDeactivation.hint: Runs when the rule is turned off.

onTrigger.title: On trigger
onTrigger.hint: Runs on a positive / raised match.

onTriggerOff.title: On trigger off
onTriggerOff.hint: Runs on a clear / leave match. Rules without a clear edge never run this.

editor.readOnly: This rule is managed by an admin. You can read it here, not change it.

problem.title: Not saved yet:
problem.name: the rule needs a name (Rule)
problem.groupingSec: the grouping window is a whole number of seconds between 5 and 60 (Rule)
problem.groupedConfirm: the AI confirm expects more than one subject, but a grouped message judges one picture per subject, so it would never send — remove the expectation (Advanced) or choose Immediate (Rule)
problem.summaryFamily: only device and system rules can be a scheduled summary — the alarm stays instant (Conditions)
problem.summaryActions: a summary never matches an event, so its actions would never run — remove them (Actions)
problem.summaryNoSendTime: a summary needs at least one send time (Conditions)
problem.summaryDegenerateWindow: a send time has no day, or its window starts and ends on the same minute — it would never be sent (Conditions)
problem.summaryActionsByAdmin: this rule has actions an administrator added; a summary never runs them, so an administrator must remove them before it can be a summary

mediaBlurb.sound: A sound owns no frame, so the picture is a photograph of the camera taken at the moment of the match — the whole scene, never a crop. The GIF and the clip are cut around the same instant, from the camera.
mediaBlurb.alarm: An alarm set off by a rule arrives with THAT rule's pictures, combined into one notification. This rule adds none of its own.

editor.enabledHint: Off keeps the rule and everything it says, but it notifies nobody until it is switched back on.
editor.usersHint: People who receive this rule on their own devices, besides the targets above. A rule needs at least one target or one user.
editor.usersUnavailable: The hub did not return its users — the list cannot be shown right now.

grouping.hint: Immediate, grouped — waits up to {{n}} s for subjects to be recognised, then sends one message with a mosaic, one picture per subject. Closes earlier when every subject is final.
grouping.plainRecognitionHint: Fires only if the name is already known when an event is written — choose Immediate, grouped to wait for it.
grouping.scopedHint: A subject not recognised within {{n}} s is not notified.
grouping.minNote: At least 5 s: subjects arriving together share one message.

editor.cooldownHint: After a notification, the same rule stays quiet for this many seconds. 0 = no pause.
editor.snoozeDefaultsHint: Not set — the notification offers the hub defaults ({{defaults}}).
editor.snoozeNoneHint: No snooze buttons: the notification cannot be silenced from the lock screen.
editor.snoozeChosenHint: Four at most. Every snooze button takes space from the rule’s action buttons.
editor.snoozeAllowGlobalHint: A snooze is personal by default. On: anyone who receives this rule can snooze it for everyone, not only for themselves.
editor.askVerdictHint: The notification carries Correct and Wrong. A tap marks the detection for retraining, the same mark as in the Library, and records who was asked and when. Channels with no buttons (email, Pushover, Gotify, WhatsApp, Discord) get the same two choices as links.

confirm.title: AI confirmation
confirm.enabledHint: A vision model looks at the picture about to be sent; the notification goes out only if it agrees.
confirm.profilesUnavailable: This hub cannot list its vision profiles — the cluster default is used.
confirm.onTimeoutLabel: If the model does not answer
confirm.onTimeoutHint: Notify anyway is the safe choice: a slow or offline model never swallows a notification.

editor.linkedCamerasHint: Every linked camera is photographed the moment the sensor fires; cameras that are offline or asleep are left out. Mosaic: one image composed from every linked camera. Each: one image per camera where the notifier accepts several, otherwise the first.
editor.clipSpeedHint: A notification GIF or clip is glanced at: at 2× the whole passage takes half the time. 1× is real time.

timezone.label: Time zone
timezone.hint: The clock the schedule windows are read on. Unset = the hub’s own time zone.
timezone.invalid: Not a known time zone — it is not saved until it is valid.

editor.snoozeExemptHint: Alarm rule: this rule concerns — or triggers — the alarm panel, and no snooze can silence it. Snooze buttons are not offered.
editor.snoozeMaxReached: At most {{max}} snooze buttons — remove one first.
editor.unlistedTargetsKept: Targets not in your list, kept on this rule: {{count}} (another user's, or deleted since). Saving never removes them.
editor.unlistedTargetsRemoved: Targets no longer available to you, removed when you save: {{count}}.

saveBlocked.roleUnknown: Couldn't confirm your account's role, so this rule can't be saved safely. Go back and open it again.
saveBlocked.targetsFailed: Couldn't load your targets, so this rule can't be saved yet. Go back and open it again.

editor.notConnected: Not connected to the hub. Reconnect and try again.
editor.hubTooOldToClear: This hub is too old to clear that field, so the change was not saved. Update CamStack on the hub, then save again.
editor.loadError: Couldn't load this rule. Go back and open it again.
editor.targetsUnavailable: Couldn't load your targets. Go back and open this again.

sensorTransition.both: It triggers and when it clears
sensorTransition.neverFires: This rule belongs to the alarm, and an alarm rule fires only when an opening OPENS. Set to “only when it clears”, it can never fire.

hint.both: Every change: water detected, and back to dry.
hint.raised: Water detected, smoke, a contact opening — never the return to normal.
hint.cleared: Back to dry, smoke gone, a contact closing — never the alert itself.

editor.sensorsEmptyWidens: No sensor selected: the rule will apply to ALL sensors.
editor.sensorsUnavailable: The hub did not return its sensors — selected ones are listed by id so they can still be removed.

systemDelivery.label: Delivery
systemDelivery.instantHint: A notification for each event, as it happens.
systemDelivery.summaryHint: Nothing is sent per event. At each time below, one notification lists what is still true for the kinds and filters of this rule — low batteries, consumables, devices or streams offline, updates available. Nothing to report sends nothing.
systemDelivery.customSchedule: Custom schedule: the summary is sent when each window below ENDS.
systemDelivery.bodyWarning: This body names none of the summary ({{token}} or a section variable) — the hub appends {{token}} to it when it sends.
systemDelivery.splitHint: One per category sends a separate notification for each category with something to report — batteries, consumables, devices offline… Needs an updated hub; an older one sends one message.
systemDelivery.splitBodyWarning: Sent one per category: this body names no {{token}}, so on every other category’s notification the hub appends {{token}} (that category’s lines).

editor.summaryNotKept: This hub does not keep scheduled summaries yet, so the rule was saved as Instant. Update the server, then set the summary again.

imageHint.scene-boxes: The whole scene at the moment of the event: the subject outlined, every other tracked object outlined thin, each with its class and confidence.
imageHint.crop: The subject cut out of the frame at the moment of the event.
imageHint.clean: The whole scene at the moment of the event, with nothing drawn on it.
imageHint.none: Send the notification with no image.

editor.showTriggerZoneLabel: Draw the zone that triggered the rule
editor.showTriggerZoneHint: Outlines the zone on the scene. Not drawn on a subject crop.
editor.showSubjectPathHint: Draws the line the subject walked, up to the moment of the picture. On a crop, only the part inside it.

kindEmpty.all: No rules yet. Create one to be told what your cameras and sensors see.
kindEmpty.detection: No detection rules yet. Create one to be told what your cameras see.
kindEmpty.sensor: No sensor rules yet. A sensor rule fires on a device event — a door opening, a switch changing.
kindEmpty.sound: No sound rules yet. A new one opens with a level threshold already set, so you only have to name the sounds and the targets.
kindEmpty.occupancy: No occupancy rules yet. A new one opens on the occupancy condition — pick the camera first, then the zone and the count.
kindEmpty.device-events: No device rules. One tells you when a device or its stream goes away or comes back, a battery runs low, or a filter, brush or mop pad needs replacing — on any device, not only cameras.
kindEmpty.system: No system rules. A system rule tells you about the installation itself — a node going offline, an addon crash-looping, an update, a backup finishing.

problem.window: Check the window — a scheduled summary needs hours, and “never longer than” has to be greater than the quiet period.
problem.barrier: The wait for tracks is between 0 and 3600 seconds.
